decision_note: Same-flower nuptial and extranuptial nectaries are used by distinct visitor guilds; the study measures pollinator bees, a nectar robber and extranuptial visitors including ants, making it a high-value functional-partition case.
Salvia floral traits and VOCs are characterized with bee visitors; anti-herbivore functions of trichomes are discussed but no focal herbivore or plant antagonist response is measured.
Focused synthesis compares regulation of floral nectar for pollination with extrafloral nectar for defence and explicitly frames reproduction-defence allocation and functional separation.
Rivea ornata directly measures pollinator dependence, effective hawkmoth visitation, florivory and reproductive success while testing attraction-reward versus florivore-defence trait allocation.
Trollius flower-shape manipulation targets an obligate pollinating seed-predator mutualism; globular flowers experience more seed predation but greater seed production and much greater pollen export.

Brassica herbivory changes floral morphology and volatiles, reduces Bombus attraction and increases parasitoid attraction across generations, directly linking antagonism to altered reproductive signalling.

Solanum study manipulates maternal herbivory and inbreeding and measures transgenerational reproduction, but offspring pollination is not a measured ecological response and seed production is generated by hand crossing.
Focused palm review explicitly synthesizes the trade-off between pollination services and antagonistic activities of other floral visitors across diverse reward and oviposition systems.

Breynia hosts two active Epicephala pollinators plus a non-pollinating seed parasite across sites, providing a direct consumer-role and partner-composition boundary in an obligate pollination mutualism.
Review concerns parasites and pathogens of bees interacting with floral products; the antagonists act on pollinators rather than as focal antagonists or exploiters of the plant.
A seed-herbivore biocontrol fly is also the most frequent effective pollinator of obligately outcrossing Bitou Bush, directly demonstrating role switching by the same consumer.
Sparattosperma floral visitors are partitioned into pollinating and nectar-thieving or robbing guilds; nearly half of visits are theft or robbery and reproductive tissues can be damaged.
Rhododendron study is a comparative elevation transcriptomic analysis and does not measure pollinator response or plant-antagonist response to a shared floral coordinate.
Trollius study quantifies the seed-predation cost of the obligate Chiastocheta pollinator-seed-predator mutualism across egg loads and populations.
Evolution item is a book review on within-plant diversity rather than an independent primary study or a focused pollinator-antagonist floral-trait synthesis.
Vegetative induction study tests resistance to insect frugivores but does not measure a pollinator response on the focal trait pathway.
Grassland grazing and nutrient-addition experiment concerns community-level plant diversity and insect abundance rather than a declared focal floral trait coordinate.
Cucumber mosaic virus changes floral volatile blends and bumblebee preference while infection changes seed yield, coupling a plant antagonist with pollinator-facing reproductive signalling.
Tabebuia floral display size is analysed against both pollinator and nectar-robber visitation across habitat disturbance, directly testing a shared display coordinate under context change.
Focused synthesis reviews visual, olfactory and nectar-taste flower aposematism as anti-florivore signalling in flowers that must also communicate with pollinators.
Handroanthus measures pollinator preference for nectar-guide states and nectar-robbing damage; robbers damage roughly two-thirds of flowers and halve fruit set.
Bromeliaceae study profiles floral VOC chemistry across species; pollination syndromes and anti-herbivore functions are interpretive context rather than measured receiver responses.
Sarracenia study links pitcher odours to captured prey composition; the focal coordinate is a carnivorous trap rather than a floral signal and no pollination response is measured.
Fynbos wand-architecture experiment tests rodent access and herbivory; pollination is discussed only as an alternative hypothesis and is not measured.
Agricultural weed-pollinator review focuses pollination-network sustainability; antagonist networks are peripheral and it is not a focused shared-trait pollinator-antagonist synthesis.
